thread:
tasha: Heads-up—noticed Console charts regressions right after yesterday's runtime push. Heatmap and sparkline frames drop, and bundle size spike on canary. Anyone actively digging?

sam: saw it on staging too. Flamegraph shows big main-thread parse time around our new telemetry import.

lee: fwiw routing/quotas changed yesterday for EU canary; could be kvcache affinity + extra telemetry tags causing larger payloads.

jordan: @sam can you paste the flamegraph snippet? also are the devtools traces showing long Scripting times or Layout?

sam: quick snippet: ```
Scripting: 620ms
Parse HTML & JS: 420ms
Layout: 110ms
Long tasks: 2 @ 250ms
```

sam: toggling off telemetry remote-fetch in local reproduces ~50% CPU drop. suspect telemetry client triggering extra network/parse.

telemetry-bot: Alert: Increased client telemetry bundle size by +18% in canary (deploy 2024-11-03T18:12Z). Error rate for chart draw ops +12%.

lee: ok that aligns. We added structured telemetry + schema validator that pulls a small polyfill. Might be causing parse bloat and a new dependency pull.

tasha: is the polyfill coming from a dynamic import or bundled inline?

lee: it's getting bundled because rollup rule didn't mark it external due to the new import path. Probable bundle regression.

jordan: aside from bundle, kvcache misses still high for heatmaps — routing policy change moved some requests to a different pool without cache affinity. That increases serial fetches and blocks the main thread when rendering tries to hydrate.

sam: reproduction steps I used: 1) enable canary 2) event with dense heatmap 3) open timeline -> see long task. I can share HAR.

jordan: actionable: revert telemetry schema change or mark polyfill external; restore previous routing affinity for heatmap routes; revert quota tweak that reduced kvcache TTL.

tasha: we need minimal blast radius. Plan: (A) revert telemetry import change in canary (quick), (B) pin routing policy for /heatmap/* to previous pool (hotfix), (C) run canary perf smoke for 30m. Agree? @deploy-bot can you hold further rollout? :pray:

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for service console-frontend. Active canary traffic frozen at 4/8 shards.

lee: I'll open a tiny PR to mark polyfill external (should be low-risk). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8421

sam: after marking external locally, bundles shrink ~15% and parse drops by ~200ms on cold load. Good signal.

jordan: I'll revert the routing affinity change on the router config and bump kvcache TTL back from 30s to 5m for heatmap endpoints. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/477

tasha: cool. Owning verification: @sam run canary perf smoke after both PRs merged, confirm LCP and main-thread long tasks drop below threshold, then we can resume rollout. Also add a perf-test job to e2e suite that simulates dense heatmap rendering.

sam: working on smoke now. ETA 20m.

telemetry-bot: Note: creating perf regression alert runbook entry — link: https://internal.redwood/ops/perf-runbooks#console-telemetry-bundle-regressions

tasha: thanks all. Quick note for post-mortem: we should add a bundling rule checklist for new imports and a small pre-merge perf check for telemetry client changes.

sam: smoke pass: main-thread long tasks down to 0-1 and parse time reduced to ~210ms on cold. Will leave canary observation for 30m then request unpause.

deploy-bot: Canary hold released on request from tasha. Rollout resumed to next batch at 1735002599.

tasha: reopening follow-up to track the checklist and perf test. I'll send calendar invite for 30m debrief. :calendar:
